title: SÈVE BOTANICALS clean-beauty launch kit: prep-and-vectorize the approved wordmark, triage the photographed foil monogram as a raster cutout, grade six mixed-light packshots to one white point, build a duotone hero texture, and data-merge one press-ready bleed label per SKU

source.reference: Modern Monochrome Logo Design + retail rollout

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a clean-beauty brand that wanted 'a fresh brand mark that feels distinctly modern' delivered 'in fully editable vector format (AI or SVG) alongside high-resolution PNGs' that 'works just as well reversed out on dark backgrounds' and 'scales cleanly from social-media avatar size to large signage.' Laundered to a fictional clean-beauty/skincare label, 'SÈVE BOTANICALS' — no real company, product, person, or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the raw brief's literal ask (DRAW a mark from scratch) is in the connector's BANNED bucket (no text-to-image, no bespoke letterform/illustration drawing), so the job is honestly scoped to the PRODUCTION half a freelancer actually runs in Adobe once a concept is approved — and SCALED UP from the killed single-mark version into the retail launch kit the brand genuinely needs: turn the approved flat wordmark scan into the editable SVG master, correctly TRIAGE a second, superficially-similar logo asset (a photographed embossed-foil monogram that must NOT be traced), grade the six product packshots that were shot across two mismatched lighting sessions (each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card) to one matched white point and knock them onto clean PDP white while preserving see-through glass, build one duotone hero texture for the landing page, and finally data-merge the six-SKU roster into the brand's authored InDesign label template to emit one press-ready, bleed-carrying label per SKU. Every deliverable is derived from a supplied input by non-generative chaining; nothing is drawn from scratch and nothing multicolor or gradient is introduced beyond the single-hue duotone the kit calls for.
one_line_ask: Prep-and-vectorize SÈVE BOTANICALS' approved flat wordmark into an editable SVG master (straighten, crisp, crop, knock-to-transparency, then trace), correctly decide that the photographed embossed-foil monogram is isolated as a raster packaging cutout and NOT vectorized, neutralize six mixed-light product packshots to the in-frame grey card each one carries so the set shares one white point, knock each onto clean PDP white without bricking the see-through glass, build one single-hue duotone hero texture, and data-merge the six-SKU roster into the authored .indd label template to produce one press-ready bleed label per SKU.
full_brief:
SÈVE BOTANICALS is a fictional modern clean-beauty and skincare label launching across social, e-commerce, unit cartons, and in-store. Our concept round is over — we have ONE approved brand mark — and now we need the whole launch kit PRODUCED in Adobe. This is a finishing/assembly job, not a from-scratch design round: do not draw anything new.

What we are handing you:
1) The approved wordmark, but only as a flat desktop SCAN on off-white paper: the word 'SÈVE BOTANICALS' set in a clean modern condensed sans with a small geometric leaf glyph above it, deep near-black ink on a slightly warm off-white ground. The scan sits a couple of degrees crooked on the bed, has extra paper margin, and the edges are a touch soft. We need this as a razor-sharp, fully editable vector (SVG) — this is the master every other logo export derives from — plus it must read clean when placed small.
2) A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of our leaf monogram debossed in metallic foil on a dark carton, with real specular glints, a slight perspective, and a soft drop shadow. We want this as a clean, isolated packaging beauty-detail asset on transparency — the real metallic foil look kept intact — for PDP and social use. Treat it as what it is: a photo of packaging, not flat line-art.
3) Six product packshots — our launch SKUs (a serum dropper, a cream jar, a cleanser tube, a rosehip face oil, a facial mist, and a balm tin) — shot over two mornings under different light: some under warm work lights, some under cooler window daylight, one or two off-level, one underexposed, one bright. We dropped a standard 18% grey card into the corner of every frame on purpose, as a neutral reference. Bring the whole set to ONE consistent, true-to-product look, using the grey card in each frame as your reference so every product's real on-shelf color is faithful and the six read as one coherent grid — a shopper scrolling should not be able to tell which morning each was shot. Hand us BOTH deliverables: first, the corrected frames with the reference grey card STILL IN VIEW (that is what lets us confirm the set is truly matched, not eyeballed); and second, the final web versions with each product knocked onto a pure solid-white PDP background, the surroundings and card gone. When you deliver, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame. On the PDP web versions keep the see-through parts see-through: the clear glass of the dropper and mist bottle, the gap under a pump, the negative space around a spatula must stay open, not filled in with solid white.
4) A botanical linen texture shot for our landing-page hero: give us one on-brand DUOTONE treatment of it — a single brand hue mapped across the tones (monochrome/tonal, not multicolor, not a gradient) — deep enough to sit type over.
5) Finally, build the shelf labels: we have hand-built the InDesign label template with real placeholder fields and image slots and proper bleed, and we are giving you the six-SKU roster. Merge them so every SKU gets its own label with its copy bound verbatim and its own matched PDP packshot dropped in, plus our brand mark in the masthead, and hand back one press-ready PDF with one label per SKU at print resolution with the bleed intact. Bind our copy exactly as written — do not rewrite names, actives, sizes or batch codes.

Hard constraints (honor the brief AND the tooling): stay monochrome/tonal on the texture — no gradients, no multicolor, no vintage/distress. No from-scratch logo drawing, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no compositing, no upscaling — every deliverable is derived from a supplied input by chaining. The requested AI/EPS exports are format-finishing layered on top of the connector-produced SVG + PNG masters.

inputs.name: seve_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'SÈVE BOTANICALS' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a clean modern condensed all-caps sans-serif reading 'SÈVE BOTANICALS' in deep near-black (#161616) ink, with a small minimal geometric leaf glyph built from a few crisp straight strokes centered above the word. Rendered as a real desktop scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (#F4F2 EC-ish, NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole lockup sits very slightly rotated about 2 degrees clockwise on the scan bed, there is generous extra paper margin around the mark, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. Strictly one ink color, no gradients, no shading, no drop shadow. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize into crisp geometric paths. High resolution 2600x2000px.
inputs.realism_notes: The APPROVED mark, supplied only as a flat scan — forces genuine prep-before-trace: it is skewed ~2deg (auto_straighten has real work), sits on a warm off-white ground (not pure white, not transparent, so a crisp adjustment + a knock-to-transparency are warranted before tracing), carries margin (crop-to-bounds matters), and is a touch soft. Feeding this raw into image_vectorize would trace the paper rectangle, the skew and doubled fuzzy edges. gemini-3-pro-image chosen for faithful, correctly-spelled logo text with hard geometric edges. This is input A of the triage pair — the FLAT CLEAN-ART one that IS vectorized.

inputs.name: seve_foil_monogram_carton.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL close-up DSLR/mirrorless camera photograph, ~4000 px long edge, of the SÈVE BOTANICALS leaf monogram DEBOSSED and foil-stamped in warm brushed gold on a dark charcoal matte skincare carton. Raking product light rakes across the foil so there are real bright specular glints and micro-scratches on the metal, the carton is shot at a slight three-quarter perspective so its edges converge, and there is a soft natural drop shadow on the surface behind it. Real cardboard texture, true metallic reflection, candid product-detail feel, no CGI gloss, no text other than the embossed glyph.
inputs.realism_notes: Input B of the triage pair — the DECOY. It looks like 'another logo asset to vectorize' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of foil with speculars, perspective and shadow. The correct treatment is to ISOLATE the carton as a raster packaging cutout (image_remove_background -> transparency, then a tight prompt-aware crop), NEVER image_vectorize — tracing it bakes the highlights, carton edges and shadow into garbage paths. Real-camera ~4000px so the tight crop stays downscale-only. Getting this triage wrong (vectorizing B, or trying to trace A without prepping) is invisible until the paths are inspected — the sanctioned failure gate.

inputs.name: seve_packshots_x6.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 6 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of SÈVE BOTANICALS skincare products, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, each product on a plain light surface. Shot across two mornings under mismatched light: (1) a CLEAR-GLASS serum bottle with a glass dropper cap (visible see-through glass and a gap under the bulb), warm tungsten work-light with an orange cast, frame tilted ~3deg; (2) a frosted CREAM JAR with a metal lid, cool window daylight, level, slightly flat; (3) an aluminium CLEANSER TUBE, warm tungsten cast, level, slightly underexposed; (4) a small amber-glass ROSEHIP FACE OIL that is GENUINELY warm amber, shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real product, not a white-balance error), level; (5) a FROSTED-GLASS FACIAL MIST bottle with a pump (see-through frosted glass, gap under the pump actuator), cool daylight, a touch bright, tilted ~3deg; (6) a brushed-metal BALM TIN, cool window light, underexposed so the metal muddies. Every shot has real product texture, glass refraction, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each. Delivered as a zip of 6 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536px raster) so each PDP crop fills the label image frame at >=300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, tilt vary) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision toward the shared white point read off its in-frame grey card. Frame 4 (rosehip oil) is THE TRAP: its warmth is real product color and its card is already neutral, so cooling it is wrong. Frames 1 and 5 carry genuine see-through glass and pump gaps — the negative space a solid-fill knockout would destroy; the correct knockout is remove_background({backgroundColor}). Frames 1/5 are tilted (auto_straighten), frame 6 is underexposed (exposure lift while holding black point).

inputs.name: seve_hero_linen_texture.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL macro camera photograph, ~4000 px long edge, of natural undyed linen fabric with a scattering of dried botanical sprigs (eucalyptus, small leaves) laid across it, soft even daylight, gentle natural shadows, full tonal range from bright fabric to shadowed folds, real woven texture and leaf detail, neutral-to-slightly-warm color, no text, no props, documentary still-life feel.
inputs.realism_notes: The landing-page hero source. Full tonal range so a single-hue monochromatic/duotone map reads with real depth. Real-camera ~4000px so any downscale to the hero export stays downscale-only. Neutral start so the desaturate + single-hue tint lands cleanly on the brand tone — this is the agent-authored tonal look, not a preset pick.

inputs.name: seve_label_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign single-record product-label template (.indd/.idml), ~2.2 x 5.5 in portrait at 300 DPI PLUS a proper 0.125 in bleed on all sides, ONE SKU per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<key_actives>>, <<size>>, <<batch_code>>, a masthead image frame wired to an @-prefixed @brandmark image column, and a primary product image frame wired to an @-prefixed @packshot image column, so the merge drops the matching PDP packshot AND the brand mark into each label. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind; explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns and produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record label is the correct, connector-doable shape (a shelf of six SKUs = six pages, one label per SKU). Two @-image columns (@packshot per-SKU, @brandmark identical every row) is a legal binding: both resolve to raster PNGs the agent produces. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. Proper bleed makes the >=300 DPI-at-trim-with-bleed acceptance gate real.

inputs.name: seve_sku_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,sku,key_actives,size,batch_code,@packshot,@brandmark holding 6 clean-beauty rows, one per launch SKU: (1) 'Clarifying Serum' / SV-SER-01 / 'Niacinamide + Zinc' / '30 ml' / 'B2601A'; (2) 'Barrier Cream' / SV-CRM-02 / 'Ceramides + Squalane' / '50 ml' / 'B2601B'; (3) 'Gentle Gel Cleanser' / SV-CLN-03 / 'Amino Acids + Aloe' / '150 ml' / 'B2601C'; (4) 'Rosehip Face Oil' / SV-OIL-04 / 'Rosehip + Vitamin E' / '20 ml' / 'B2601D'; (5) 'Hydrating Facial Mist' / SV-MST-05 / 'Panthenol + Rose Water' / '100 ml' / 'B2601E'; (6) 'Repair Balm' / SV-BLM-06 / 'Shea + Bisabolol' / '15 ml' / 'B2601F'. The @packshot column names each SKU's matched PDP packshot file (e.g. @seve_serum_pdp.png); the @brandmark column names the same cleaned wordmark PNG on every row so the masthead mark is identical across the shelf. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<product_name>>,<<sku>>,<<key_actives>>,<<size>>,<<batch_code>> and the @packshot / @brandmark image columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Headers match the authored .indd fields and both @-image columns so the one-file-per-row merge binds copy AND the correct images per SKU. Six rows => the merge must produce EXACTLY six finished labels (page-count=row-count=6). The @packshot column is the binding contract: the agent must point it at its OWN produced PDP packshots. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool here (cannot bind the image columns).

outputs.name: seve_master_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Clean, fully editable vector MASTER of the SÈVE BOTANICALS wordmark + leaf glyph, traced ONLY after the flat scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark's true bounds, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp geometric paths on a transparent ground with no captured paper rectangle and no baked-in skew. The scalable master from which the AI/EPS + high-res PNG exports derive. Strictly monochrome. DELIVERABLE 1 (the vectorize_logo core).

outputs.name: seve_foil_carton_cutout.png
outputs.spec: The photographed embossed-foil monogram carton ISOLATED onto transparency as a raster packaging cutout (image_remove_background -> transparency, then a tight prompt-aware crop), preserving the real metallic speculars and drop shadow of the foil — deliberately NOT vectorized. A hi-res transparent PNG packaging beauty-detail for PDP/social use. DELIVERABLE 2 (the correct triage treatment of decoy input B).

outputs.name: seve_packshots_neutralized_masters_x6
outputs.spec: Six RETAINED card-bearing neutralized MASTERS — the six packshots after their per-frame white-balance + exposure correction, exported/retained with the in-frame 18% grey card STILL IN FRAME and BEFORE any knockout or crop (these are the neutralize outputs serum_neutralized / cream_neutralized / cleanser_neutralized / rosehip_neutralized / mist_neutralized / balm_neutralized from workflow steps 9/12/15/18/22/25). This is the artifact grey-card NEUTRALITY is graded on, because the delivered PDP crop below has the card cropped out. sRGB, retained at native/downscaled scale (never upscaled past source). Acceptance (grader-checked): in every master the in-frame grey card reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) with no channel clipped to 0/255, and all six masters share ONE white point and brightness (a common neutral read off the six cards). The agent neutralizes each card BY EYE and REPORTS the temp/tint/exposure it APPLIED per frame — it never reads a pixel value. DELIVERABLE 3a (the card-bearing grading master; pairs with seve_grade_report).

outputs.name: seve_pdp_packshots_x6
outputs.spec: Six card-cropped PDP web packshots (serum, cream jar, cleanser tube, rosehip oil, facial mist, balm tin), each derived from its retained card-bearing master (above) by knocking the product onto pure solid-white (#FFFFFF) PDP background with the surround AND the grey card gone, and ALL see-through negative space (clear dropper glass, frosted-mist glass, gap under the pump) preserved — NOT solid-filled/bricked. sRGB PNG, long edge ~2048 px, and at least 300 effective DPI at the label image-frame trim. Acceptance (grader-checked): the grey card and surround are fully EXCLUDED from every delivered crop (this file is checked for card EXCLUSION and preserved negative space — NOT for card neutrality, which is graded on the retained card-bearing master seve_packshots_neutralized_masters_x6, never on this file the card is cropped from); every see-through region stays open/transparent, not bricked; the set reads as one matched white point inherited from the masters. DELIVERABLE 3b (also the six @packshot cells the merge binds).

outputs.name: seve_hero_duotone_texture.png
outputs.spec: One on-brand single-hue DUOTONE/tonal treatment of the linen-and-botanicals hero source: desaturated and contrast-shaped from primitives, then mapped to a single brand hue across the tonal range (monochromatic tint — one hue only, no multicolor, no gradient), deep enough to carry overlaid type. Hi-res sRGB PNG for the landing-page hero. DELIVERABLE 4.

outputs.name: seve_labels_perSKU_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly six press-ready product labels — ONE single-record label per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) — produced by merging seve_sku_roster.csv into the AUTHORED seve_label_template.indd via document_merge_data_layout and exporting via document_render_layout: each label binds its <<product_name>>/<<sku>>/<<key_actives>>/<<size>>/<<batch_code>> verbatim from the roster, drops that SKU's matched PDP packshot into the @packshot frame and the brand mark into the @brandmark masthead frame. Acceptance (grader-checked): label/page count == data row count == 6 (a broken or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed packshot renders at >=300 DPI at the label trim; the 0.125 in bleed is present on the exported PDF. DELIVERABLE 5 (the owned composed endpoint).

outputs.name: seve_grade_report
outputs.spec: A short parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the six packshots, the final white-balance (temperature / tint) and exposure move it APPLIED, plus the single shared house white point all six were matched to. Pairs with the retained card-bearing masters (seve_packshots_neutralized_masters_x6) — the report logs the applied corrections while the grader measures the grey card on the masters — so 'the set is matched to one target' is checkable. The reported corrections must be non-identical across the warm vs cool frames (and must show white balance HELD on the genuinely-amber rosehip frame). This is a report of APPLIED settings, never a measured/read pixel value.

connector_workflow.note: Prep-before-trace step 1 (input A, the FLAT scan): the mark sits ~2deg rotated on the scan bed — straighten so the vector edges come out square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake the rotation into the paths.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the warm off-white paper toward white so the near-black lettering and leaf glyph separate hard from the ground. A soft, low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges. Primitives only (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_brightness_and_contrast).
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the lockup so vectorize traces only the mark, not the surrounding paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to true transparency so the trace captures the letterforms + glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). This transparent PNG also serves as the @brandmark image bound into every label masthead.

Now trace the PREPARED raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into the clean editable SVG MASTER. DELIVERABLE 1. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. This is the FLAT-ART branch of the triage.

TRIAGE — the DECOY branch (input B). This is a PHOTOGRAPH of foil (speculars, perspective, shadow), so the correct move is to ISOLATE it as a raster, NOT vectorize it. remove_background lifts the carton onto transparency, keeping the real metallic reflection and drop shadow intact. Feeding B to image_vectorize would trace the highlights and carton edges into garbage paths — the sanctioned wrong decision.

Tight prompt-aware crop of the isolated foil-monogram carton to a clean centered packaging-detail cutout. DELIVERABLE 2. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'), downscale-only from the ~4000px source, never enlarging beyond source pixels. Confirms the decoy became a photographic raster asset, not a vector.
Packshot 1 (serum, Session A warm, tilted ~3deg): level it first. Triage — only the tilted frames 1 and 5 get straightened; the level frames skip this.

Serum, warm tungsten cast: COOL the temperature and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral, then set exposure to the shared brightness target. Reason the exact temp/exposure to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitives call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature). This corrected frame — grey card STILL IN FRAME — is RETAINED as a card-bearing neutralized master (deliverable seve_packshots_neutralized_masters_x6); grey-card neutrality is graded HERE, before step 10's knockout crops the card out.

Knock the serum onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}). CORRECT knockout path: it isolates the bottle, removes the surround AND the grey card, and preserves the see-through DROPPER GLASS and the gap under the bulb as clean white. Because this removes the grey card, the resulting PDP crop is card-EXCLUDED by design — grey-card neutrality was already locked upstream and is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing master serum_neutralized (card in frame), never on this card-cropped crop; the crop is checked only for card exclusion + preserved negative space. Deliberately NOT select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area: select_subject mis-fires on a product still-life and fill_area solids the whole mask, bricking the clear glass — the exact failure the brief calls out.

Crop+resize the isolated serum to the shared PDP spec (long edge ~2048px, sRGB, >=300 DPI at the label frame). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and the @packshot cell for SV-SER-01.

Cream jar (Session B cool daylight, level, flat): WARM the temperature to neutralize its grey card to the SHARED white point and add a little contrast — the OPPOSITE WB direction from the warm serum. The trap is applying one correction to all six. Report the move. Retain this corrected frame (card in frame) as a card-bearing neutralized master for grading, before the knockout.
Knock the cream jar onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); preserve the negative space around the lid. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 10.
Crop+resize the cream jar to the shared PDP spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @packshot cell for SV-CRM-02.

Cleanser tube (Session A warm, level, slightly under): cool the WB to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point AND lift exposure to the set brightness. Warm like the serum but a different exposure, so its numbers are close but NOT copied. Report the move. Retain this corrected frame (card in frame) as a card-bearing neutralized master for grading, before the knockout.
Knock the cleanser tube onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); preserve any negative space around the cap.
Crop+resize the cleanser tube to the shared PDP spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @packshot cell for SV-CLN-03.

THE TRAP FRAME. The rosehip oil is GENUINELY amber and was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' move used on frames 1/3, or 'cools an imagined cast', neutralizes the card off-neutral and strips the product's real amber. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was HELD. Retain this corrected frame (card in frame) as a card-bearing neutralized master for grading, before the knockout — the grader confirms the rosehip card is neutral here while the product's real amber is preserved.
Knock the rosehip oil onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); the amber glass is translucent, so preserve its see-through character rather than bricking it solid.
Crop+resize the rosehip oil to the shared PDP spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @packshot cell for SV-OIL-04.
Packshot 5 (facial mist, Session B cool, bright, tilted ~3deg): level it first.

Facial mist (cool cast, bright): WARM the WB to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point AND pull exposure DOWN — cool like the cream jar but brighter, so a different exposure direction. Report the move. Retain this corrected frame (card in frame) as a card-bearing neutralized master for grading, before the knockout.

Knock the mist bottle onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); preserve the see-through FROSTED GLASS and the gap under the PUMP actuator — the second negative-space case a fill_area knockout would destroy.
Crop+resize the mist bottle to the shared PDP spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @packshot cell for SV-MST-05.

Balm tin (Session B cool, underexposed): warm the WB to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point AND LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the brushed metal does not crush to 0 or wash to grey. Dominant move here is tonal, not just WB. Report the move. Retain this corrected frame (card in frame) as a card-bearing neutralized master for grading, before the knockout.
Knock the balm tin onto solid-white PDP via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); preserve the negative space around the lid seam.

Crop+resize the balm tin to the shared PDP spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @packshot cell for SV-BLM-06. Steps 8-27 produce BOTH the six RETAINED card-bearing neutralized masters (the neutralize outputs serum_neutralized/cream_neutralized/cleanser_neutralized/rosehip_neutralized/mist_neutralized/balm_neutralized, grey card still in frame — deliverable seve_packshots_neutralized_masters_x6, where neutrality is graded) and the six card-cropped seve_pdp_packshots_x6 web crops (card EXCLUDED, negative space preserved — also the six @packshot cells the merge binds) — all six neutralized to their own grey card so the masters share one white point.

Duotone hero step 1: desaturate the linen-and-botanicals texture to a full-range monochrome base and shape contrast so the shadows are deep enough to carry overlaid type. Authored from primitives — the base for the single-hue map, not a preset.

Duotone hero step 2: map the monochrome base to a SINGLE brand hue across the tonal range (one hue only — no multicolor, no gradient), producing the on-brand tonal hero background. DELIVERABLE 4. Single tone honors the monochrome-only rule; this is not a repeated-at-N-hues variant stack.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: seve_serum_pdp.png, seve_cream_pdp.png, seve_cleanser_pdp.png, seve_rosehip_pdp.png, seve_mist_pdp.png, seve_balm_pdp.png, seve_wordmark_knockout
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six matched PDP packshots plus the cleaned wordmark PNG so the merge can reference them by the @packshot and @brandmark columns. Plumbing — not counted as difficulty.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @packshot column resolves to per SKU and the @brandmark column resolves to for every masthead. Plumbing.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the six roster rows (product_name/sku/key_actives/size/batch_code) into the authored single-record .indd's live <<fields>>, drop that row's matched PDP packshot into the @packshot frame and the cleaned wordmark into the @brandmark masthead frame. Emits EXACTLY one merged label per row (six labels).
